deep.reconstruction:
The page is not by Riemann. It is in Dedekind's hand: the draft of his 'Erläuterungen zu den vorstehenden Fragmenten', which was printed in Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1876) after the fragments on the limiting behaviour of the elliptic modular functions.

(1) Historical remarks. Riemann's first fragment dates from September 1852. Dedekind conjectures that Riemann wanted examples, for the trigonometric-series Habilitationsschrift, of functions that are discontinuous infinitely often in every interval. The second, barely legible sheet may have had the same aim. Riemann's method studies the modular functions of elliptic-function theory as the period ratio approaches a rational value. The period ratio is omega = K'i/K = log(q)/(pi i), with q = e^{-pi K'/K} = e^{pi i omega}.

Dedekind's own remark is that this method also yields the constants (eighth roots of unity) in the first-order transformation of the theta functions. Jacobi and Hermite had reduced these constants to Gauss sums, hence to quadratic residues. He says he noticed this only in the last days before printing and could not check all of Riemann's formulas.

(2) Definition. Dedekind declares the centre of the theory of these modular functions, which can be built independently of elliptic functions. Writing 1^z := e^{2 pi i z}, he defines
 eta(omega) = 1^{omega/24} * prod_{nu>=1} (1 - 1^{omega nu}) = q^{1/12} * prod_{nu>=1} (1 - q^{2 nu}).

The two forms agree; the check is mine:
- 1^{omega/24} = e^{pi i omega/12} = q^{1/12}.
- 1^{omega nu} = e^{2 pi i omega nu} = q^{2 nu}.

This is the modern Dedekind eta function eta(tau), with tau = omega in the upper half plane.

(3) Crossed-out draft (right column). This is an earlier formulation of the same definition. eta is given as a function of omega = x + iy, defined for all positive y. A branch of log eta(omega) is fixed by requiring log eta(omega) - omega pi i/12 -> 0 as y -> infinity, i.e. as q -> 0. The next page adopts exactly this normalisation.

The next page goes on to quote Jacobi's relations (Fundamenta nova §36) linking eta(2 omega), eta(omega/2), eta((1+omega)/2) to k, k' and 2K/pi.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. omega = K'i/K = log q/(pi i) is consistent with q = e^{-pi K'/K}, and the two expressions for eta(omega) agree.
Attribution caveat: the handwriting and content are Dedekind's commentary, not Riemann's own work.

results.what: Definition eta(omega) = e^{pi i omega/12} prod(1 - e^{2 pi i nu omega}), with branch of log eta normalised by log eta - pi i omega/12 -> 0 as Im omega -> infinity
results.usually_credited_to: R. Dedekind, 1876/77 (commentary in Riemann's Werke and Crelle 83)

results.what: Riemann's method of determining the behaviour of modular functions as omega approaches a rational real value (Grenzfälle der elliptischen Modulfunctionen)
results.modern_name: Behaviour of modular forms at cusps; Riemann's fragment on limiting cases, precursor of Dedekind sums
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (fragment, 1852, published 1876), worked out by Dedekind

results.what: Remark that this method determines the root-of-unity constants in the first-order theta transformation, previously reduced to Gauss sums
results.modern_name: Eta/theta multiplier system; later Dedekind sums and the transformation formula for log eta
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi and Hermite (Gauss-sum evaluation); Dedekind 1876 (eta transformation via this method)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is Dedekind's draft of his well-known published commentary, which introduced the eta function and led to Dedekind sums. Everything here appears in Riemann's Werke (1876) under Dedekind's name, and nothing is a new Riemann result.

checkable.asserts: The two expressions for eta(omega) on the page agree (numerically about 0).

checkable.sympy: Kr = Symbol('Kr', positive=True); q = exp(-pi*Kr); simplify(log(q)/(pi*I) - I*Kr)
checkable.asserts: omega = K'i/K = log q/(pi i) when q = exp(-pi K'/K); here Kr = K'/K.

checkable.sympy: eta = lambda w: exp(pi*I*w/12)*Product(1-exp(2*pi*I*w*n),(n,1,80)).doit(); w = Rational(1,3)+I*Rational(9,10); N(eta(2*w)*eta(w/2)*eta((1+w)/2) - exp(pi*I/24)*eta(w)**3)
checkable.asserts: Jacobi's relation eta(2w)eta(w/2)eta((1+w)/2) = 1^{1/48} eta(w)^3, quoted on the next page and underlying the log normalisation (about 0).
log eta(omega) - pi i omega/12 is small for large Im omega, matching the normalisation in the crossed-out text.

transcription_corrections: The hand is Dedekind's, as the heading 'Erläuterungen ... von R. Dedekind' states; this is not a Riemann autograph.
In 'die Correctheit [-aller-] {+der+} Riemann'schen Formeln', 'der' is written in the left margin replacing the struck 'aller'. The transcription is essentially right.

In the crossed-out right column, 'alle' is an interlinear insertion above a struck word (probably 'positiven'). A reading like 'für {+alle+} [-positiven?-] Werthe von y' is more faithful than 'alle positiven'.
The struck word before 'Constanten' looks like 'Modulfu...' / 'Moduln', so the reading is plausible but uncertain.
